This study investigates the stability of quantization and extraction methods in the context of developing lightweight, low-resource machine translation models. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that leverages weakly annotated data to train a model for COVID-19 lesion localization and segmentation. Our method utilizes a weakly guided learning framework that combines a weakly annotated dataset with a small set of fully annotated data to train a model that can accurately localize and segment COVID-19 lesions. Our experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, and can be applied to other medical imaging tasks.
